title: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Triage Agent remediation reminders in Teams
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, opt-in default, licensing and administrative controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes the documented preview from the roadmap targets and reports both Microsoft's immediate-block guidance and Teams' availability-change delay.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Purview's Data Security Triage Agent and Teams remediation.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Triage Agent - Sensitive Data Remediation through Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is December CY2027, presented as a target rather than a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The record lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": [ "General Availability", "Preview" ]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": [ "Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)" ]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": [ "Web" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap record does not list US Government clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": [ "Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap description promises administrative visibility through the Data Security Posture Management dashboard.
claims.quote: giving admins real-time visibility and control via the Data Security Posture Management dashboard

claims.claim: Remediation reminders apply to SharePoint and OneDrive alerts triaged as Needs attention.
claims.quote: For Sharepoint/OneDrive alerts triaged as Needs Attention, the agent sends a Microsoft Teams chat to the last modified user of the file

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The recipient of the Teams message is the user who last modified the file.
claims.quote: Reminders are sent once daily to the user who is last modifier of the file in context

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The agent asks the user to remove sensitive information rather than removing it itself.
claims.quote: the agent sends a Microsoft Teams chat to the last modified user of the file, and ask them to remove the sensitive information found in the file related to the alert. (Preview)

claims.claim: Learn documents remediation reminders as preview and warns that the steps and feature may change.
claims.quote: Remediation reminders for the Data Security Triage Agent are currently in **Preview**. Features and steps described in this article might change before general availability.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Reminders are sent once daily.
claims.quote: Reminders are sent once daily to the user who is last modifier of the file in context

claims.claim: A reminder can combine up to 10 files requiring remediation.
claims.quote: (combining up to 10 files if multiple files require remediation)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Each remediation message includes the file name.
claims.quote: The remediation message includes the file name and a description of what sensitive information requires attention.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Each remediation message describes the sensitive information requiring attention.
claims.quote: The remediation message includes the file name and a description of what sensitive information requires attention.

claims.claim: A remediated file is removed from the following day's reminder.
claims.quote: Once the last person who modified, remediates the file, the file is removed from the remediation reminder for the next day.

claims.claim: No reminder is sent when there are no files left for the reminder.
claims.quote: If no files are found, no reminder is sent.

claims.claim: Enabling remediation reminders also enables the Teams bot for the tenant.
claims.quote: Enabling this setting also enables the bot in Microsoft Teams for the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The DLP Triage Agent alert queue displays alert-level remediation progress.
claims.quote: You can view remediation status at the alert level on the Triage Agent alert queue in the DLP solution.

claims.claim: Fully remediated means users have remediated all files implicated in the alert.
claims.quote: This view lets a user see fully remediated alerts, meaning users remediated all files implicated in the alert.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: In progress indicates outreach occurred but not all files have been remediated.
claims.quote: *In progress* means that the Agent reached out to the user, but the user didn't remediate all the files yet.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Error indicates that the Teams message could not be sent.
claims.quote: *Error* indicates that the Teams message couldn't be sent.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Each alert's Related assets section displays the individual files' remediation status.
claims.quote: You can see the status inside each DLP alert in the *Related assets* section that lists all the files implicated in the alert and the respective remediation status.

claims.claim: The cited Learn setup page does not describe the roadmap's DSPM dashboard view of remediation progress.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Data Security Triage Agent remediation progress Data Security Posture Management dashboard; read the cited get-started page in full and searched its text for Posture and dashboard; it describes the DLP alert queue and Related assets, not that dashboard.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in: one-click setup turns reminders off and configuration is required before delivery.
claims.quote:
The default settings for 'One-Click' setup are:

- Identity: Create and use agent identity
- Trigger: Run automatically based on a set schedule
- Alert timeframe: Triage alerts from the last 30 days
- Remediation reminder: Turned OFF (Preview)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects the documented requirement for both per-seat licensing and pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: This agent requires [both the standard per seat licensing model and the pay-as-you-go billing model](purview-billing-models).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The organisation must be licensed for Microsoft Data Loss Prevention to use the DLP triage agent.
claims.quote:
Your organization must be licensed for:

- Microsoft Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to use the DLP triage agent.

claims.where: front matter: cost; summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The triage agent consumes security compute units as it performs its tasks, independently of enabling remediation.
claims.quote: The agent consumes security compute units (SCUs) as it performs its tasks.

claims.claim: SCUs must be provisioned for the triage agent to work.
claims.quote: You must have SCUs provisioned for the triage agent to work.

claims.claim: SCU consumption depends on the number and type of alerts processed.
claims.quote: The number of SCUs consumed depends on the number and type of alerts that are processed.

claims.claim: The preview remediation capability costs nothing extra beyond the SCUs needed to triage the alert first.
claims.quote: The Remediation Capability doesn't cost anything extra. The only costs associated with using this capability are the SCUs needed to triage the DLP alert first.

claims.claim: Provisioned Security Copilot capacity is billed by the hour.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour while the overage capacity is billed on usage.

claims.claim: Security Copilot overage capacity is billed on usage.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour while the overage capacity is billed on usage.

claims.claim: Overage units can be configured as unlimited or with a maximum amount.
claims.quote: Overage units are billed on-demand and can be set as unlimited or a maximum amount.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The capacity page documents automatically created inclusion capacity when inclusion is enabled through Microsoft 365 E5 and E7.
claims.quote: **Default Security Copilot Capacity** is the automatically created inclusion capacity that appears in your tenant when Security Copilot inclusion is enabled through Microsoft 365 E5 and E7.

claims.claim: Microsoft points readers to Security Copilot pricing and the pricing calculator for SCU pricing.
claims.quote: For more information, see [Microsoft Security Copilot pricing](https://aka.ms/CopilotforSecurity_Pricing) and the [Pricing calculator](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/calculator/?service=microsoft-copilot-for-security) page.

claims.claim: Policies enabled for remediation are always a subset of policies enabled for triage.
claims.quote: Policies enabled for remediation are always a subset of policies enabled for triage.

claims.claim: The agent can be assigned an Agent Identity that allows data access and actions.
claims.quote: The agent is assigned **Agent Identity**, which allows it to access data and take actions

claims.claim: The agent can instead be set up using the identity of the user setting it up.
claims.quote: or can be set up by assigning the user's identity who is setting the agent.

claims.claim: Purview automatically installs the Teams app for a user when a remediation message is sent.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview automatically installs the app for a specific user at the time a remediation message is sent.

claims.claim: The app needs to be available rather than preinstalled for users.
claims.quote: The Data Security Triage Agent app doesn't need to be preinstalled for users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The agent triages alerts only from active-mode DLP policies, not policies in simulation mode.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP only supports alerts from policies that are in active mode. It doesn't triage alerts from DLP policies that are running in simulation mode.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Delivery requires both the org-wide Microsoft apps setting and the agent app's availability to be correctly configured.
claims.quote: Two settings must be correctly configured for the Data Security Triage Agent to send remediation messages through Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Microsoft identifies org-wide Microsoft apps enabled but the individual agent app blocked as a common misconfiguration.
claims.quote: A common misconfiguration occurs when the org-wide Microsoft apps toggle is *enabled* but the Data Security Triage Agent app is *individually blocked*.

claims.where: controls[2].note; controls[3].note; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Configuring the Teams settings requires Teams admin permissions.
claims.quote: You must have [Teams admin permissions](/en-us/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles) to configure the Microsoft Teams Admin Center settings described in this article.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Purview admin configuring the agent may lack the Teams admin permissions needed for the Teams settings.
claims.quote: The Purview admin or analyst who configures the triage agent might not have permissions to access the Microsoft Teams Admin Center.

claims.claim: Only one instance of each agent can exist in a tenant.
claims.quote: There can be only one instance of each agent in a tenant, regardless of the portal in which it was deployed.

claims.claim: The triage agent can be deployed from either Purview or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: The Triage Agent can be deployed from both Microsoft Purview and Defender XDR portals

claims.claim: The deployed agent can be managed, edited and disabled only from the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: The Triage Agent can be deployed from both Microsoft Purview and Defender XDR portals, but can only be managed, edited, and disabled from the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The tenant must be onboarded to Microsoft Security Copilot.
claims.quote: Your tenant must be onboarded to Microsoft Security Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 data sharing must be enabled in Security Copilot.
claims.quote: You must enable Microsoft 365 data sharing in Security Copilot.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview plug-in must be enabled in Security Copilot.
claims.quote: You must enable the Microsoft Purview plug-in in Microsoft Security Copilot.

claims.claim: The Purview path is Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > Edit agent > Agent configuration > Remediation reminders in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: Select **Agent configuration** for editing and configuring settings like Trigger, alert timeframe, remediation reminders, reminder duration, and policy scope.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for setting the agent's remediation reminders or reminder duration.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Security Compliance PowerShell DLP Triage Agent remediation reminders policy scope configuration cmdlets; Purview triage agent remediation reminders policy scope PowerShell Security Compliance API configure. Read the setup and Teams configuration pages; no such operation found.

claims.claim: The Purview policy scope path is Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > Edit agent > Agent configuration > Set agent scope > Edit > Select policies > Remediation.
claims.quote:
Under **Set agent scope**, select **Edit**.
5. In the **Select policies** panel, enable the **Remediation** toggle only for the policies where you want remediation messages sent to users.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for selecting which agent-scope policies send remediation messages.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Security Compliance PowerShell DLP Triage Agent remediation reminders policy scope configuration cmdlets. Read setup and Teams configuration pages and Set-DlpCompliancePolicy search excerpts; no operation setting agent remediation scope found.

claims.claim: The Teams path is Teams apps > Manage apps > Data Security Triage Agent > Users and groups > Edit availability.
claims.quote:
Go to **Teams apps** > **Manage apps**.
3. Search for **Data Security Triage Agent** and select it.
4. Go to the **Users and groups** tab.
5. Select **Edit availability**.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets the identified Teams app's availability to everyone.
claims.quote: PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone

claims.claim: The required Microsoft apps toggle is at Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps.
claims.quote:
Go to **Teams apps** > **Manage apps**.
3. Select **Actions** > **Org-wide app settings**.
4. In the **Org-wide app settings** panel, set the **Microsoft apps** toggle to **On**.

claims.claim: No automation operation was found for the org-wide Microsoft apps toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide Microsoft apps toggle Graph API PowerShell TeamsAppSettings; Teams org-wide app settings Microsoft apps toggle PowerShell Set-CsTeamsAppPermissionPolicy DefaultCatalogAppsType. Read Teams configuration and beta teamsAppSettings; no operation for this toggle found.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Purview deactivation path is Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > ellipses (three dots) > Deactivate agent.
claims.quote:
select the ellipses (three dots) that are located *next to* the **Edit agent** button.
6. Select **Deactivate agent**. Deactivating the agent stops the agent from triaging alerts.

claims.claim: No automation operation was found for deactivating this agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview triage agent deactivate API PowerShell SCU usage monitoring API; Security Copilot Purview triage agent SCU usage monitoring export API PowerShell deactivate. Read get-started Deactivate agents and returned deployment excerpts; no deactivation operation found.

claims.where: controls[5].ui; Governance controls table; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Purview usage path is Agents > Explore agents > View agent > Edit agent > Usage monitoring.
claims.quote:
select **Agents**.
3. Select **Explore agents**.
4. Select **View agent** for agent you want to edit.
5. Select **Edit agent**.
6. Select **Usage monitoring**.

claims.claim: No automation operation was found for this agent's SCU usage-monitoring control.
claims.quote: Searched: Security Copilot Purview triage agent SCU usage monitoring export API PowerShell deactivate; Purview triage agent deactivate API PowerShell SCU usage monitoring API. Read get-started Monitor SCU usage and returned usage/deployment excerpts; no equivalent operation found.

claims.claim: Blocking the agent app for a user prevents a generated remediation message from being sent to that user.
claims.quote: Blocking the app for a user is a hard block. Even if an alert is triaged and a remediation message is generated, the message *won't* be sent to users for whom the app is blocked.

claims.claim: The feature-specific Teams page says setting availability to No one immediately stops all remediation messages.
claims.quote: This result is a failsafe mechanism--if you need to *immediately* stop all remediation messages, set availability to **No one**.

claims.claim: Everyone makes the Teams app available to all users.
claims.quote: | `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.claim: General Teams guidance says UI or PowerShell availability changes can take up to 24 hours to apply to all users.
claims.quote: UI or PowerShell changes take up to 24 hours to apply to all users, consistent with anytime UI or PowerShell updates occur, not just immediately after migration completion.

claims.claim: Reminder duration configures how many days the agent follows up about unremediated files.
claims.quote: Select **Reminder duration**, which is the number of days the agent sends the reminders on Microsoft Teams for a particular file requiring action from last modified user. (Preview)

claims.claim: Deactivation stops alert triage without removing the agent.
claims.quote: Deactivating the agent stops the agent from triaging alerts. It doesn't remove the agent

claims.where: controls[5].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Usage monitoring tracks SCU consumption through Security Copilot's monitoring tool rather than setting a spending limit.
claims.quote: You can track your SCU consumption in the [usage monitoring tool](/en-us/copilot/security/manage-usage).

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends policy scoping for routine control of files and locations, with Teams blocking as an additional safeguard.
claims.quote: Use policy scoping in Purview for routine control over what files and locations trigger remediation. Use Teams Admin Center blocking as another safeguard

claims.claim: The triage agent as a whole supports alerts from Exchange, Devices, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP triages alerts from Exchange, Devices, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams.
